newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FIRST AFRIKAANS TALK RADIO APPLIES FOR LICENCE.
newsitem.headline: FIRST AFRIKAANS TALK RADIO APPLIES FOR LICENCE.

text.p: A diversified local consortium, Punt Media, said it had applied on Wednesday for a new South African radio license which would enable it to be the country's first Afrikaans talk radio station.
The total investment would amount to 12 million rand.
The application for a medium wave frequency in the Western Cape was made on Wednesday and a further application for a Gauteng medium wave frequency will be heard on December 4.
Andre Potgieter, whose company comprises 20 percent of the bidding consortium, said in a statement:

"The scaling down of Afrikaans on SABC radio and television has engendered a sense of loss amongst Afrikaners. We hope to normalise one of the most contentious aspects in our history by re-establishing Afrikaans as a muscular, soulful, passionate and diversified language."

Punt Media said that if both medium wave frequencies were granted, the radio station could break even in its second year of operation. If only the Cape licence was granted then it would take five years to break even.

Other members of the consortium are: Boland Financial Services (20 percent), Genbel Securities (20 percent) and black empowerment groupings Mnyama Holdings (10 percent) and Nozala Investments (30 percent).
South Africa currently has only one talk radio station, English medium Radio 702.
